topic: DFI fault codes (blink codes)
statement: 2019-2023 Kawasaki KX450. When the fuel injection system has a fault, the bike flashes a two-digit service code as long and short blinks: read the tens digit, then the ones digit. Codes: 11 throttle sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 12 intake air pressure sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 13 intake air temperature sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 14 water temperature sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 21 crankshaft sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 25 gear position switch fault or its wiring open or shorted; 31 vehicle-down (tip-over) sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 41 fuel injector fault or its wiring open or shorted; 46 fuel pump fault or its wiring open or shorted; 51 ignition coil fault or its wiring open or shorted; 7F battery voltage abnormal. topic: Battery, charging and main fuse
statement: 2025-2027 Kawasaki KX250. Battery: 12.8 V, 2.0 Ah lithium-ion. Charge only with a charger made for lithium batteries, never a lead-acid charger: 13.9 to 14.9 V at 1 A. Check the battery before riding or every two weeks and charge it when it reads under 12.8 V. Main fuse: 10 A behind the right radiator shroud, with a spare. Disconnect the battery negative cable before pulling it. A blown main fuse means the starter does nothing.
notes: From Kawasaki's owner's manual for this model year. The wire-by-wire diagram is printed in the manual and is not reproduced here.

topic: DFI fault codes (blink codes)
statement: 2025-2027 Kawasaki KX250. When the fuel injection system has a fault, the bike flashes a two-digit service code as long and short blinks: read the tens digit, then the ones digit. Several stored codes play lowest number first. Codes: 11 throttle sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 12 intake air pressure sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 13 intake air temperature sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 14 water temperature sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 21 crankshaft sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 25 gear position switch fault or its wiring open or shorted; 31 vehicle-down (tip-over) sensor fault or its wiring open or shorted; 41 downstream injector fault or its wiring open or shorted; 42 upstream injector fault or its wiring open or shorted; 46 fuel pump fault or its wiring open or shorted; 51 ignition coil fault or its wiring open or shorted; 75 main relay fault or its wiring open or shorted; 7F battery voltage abnormal. If the part and its wiring check good, check the ECU power and ground before blaming the ECU.
notes: From Kawasaki's owner's manual for this model year. The wire-by-wire diagram is printed in the manual and is not reproduced here.

topic: Engine map selection and launch control
statement: 2025-2027 Kawasaki KX250. Power mode (full or mild) and KTRC traction control (off, mode 1 or the stronger mode 2) are set with the two handlebar buttons, with the throttle closed and the engine idling. Custom fuel and ignition settings are made in the Rideology app through the communication unit on the bike. Launch control: engine running in neutral, 1st or 2nd, press both buttons together and the left indicator turns purple. It blinks slowly from 10,000 to 13,000 rpm and fast at 13,000 rpm or more. It switches off when you shift into 3rd.
notes: From Kawasaki's owner's manual for this model year. The wire-by-wire diagram is printed in the manual and is not reproduced here.
